name: Yaesu FT-277R
notes: Stock, unmodified FT-277R. A MARS/CAP-modded radio transmits outside the amateur allocation and is a separate target: use yaesu_ft277_mars. 70 cm sibling of the FT-270R: same chassis, keypad, menu tree and clone protocol, different RF deck. Bench-verified 2026-09-13 against a physical radio (Chicago-Offline ft270-277-info, dumps/ft277r-2026-09-13-read.md): the radio reports model ID 'AH022U', so stock CHIRP programs it as a Yaesu VX-177 with no patch, and the clone image is the FT-7800-family format at 6057 bytes with valid checksums. Channel storage limits are the VX-177 driver's, inherited from VX170Radio (chirp/drivers/vx170.py): memory_bounds (1, 200) and names[200] with char name[6], so display names are six characters. modes is ["FM"] (driver MODES ["FM", "NFM"], no AM) and bandwidths_khz 12.5/25 follows that split. The TX band is the US amateur 70 cm allocation 430-450 MHz; the wider 420-470 MHz span is the driver's valid_bands and is rx_only here because stock firmware will not transmit outside the ham band. That rules out GMRS/FRS (462-467 MHz) on a stock radio even though the receiver tunes there. max_zones is 1 as a profile-0.1 compatibility shim; the driver sets has_bank = False, so memory banks are unreachable through CHIRP. Write path: CHIRP.app GUI upload, verified 2026-09-13 on a physical radio; cable is the RT Systems CT57B at 9600 baud. Never write an FT-270R image into this radio: the two images are the same size and differ by one byte in the model ID, and CHIRP's model check is the only guard against putting 2 m data in front of a 70 cm PA.
